summary: Reviewed workflow-next-action.ts (Priority 3d ROUTE_PIPELINE_AGENT block, lines 462–504) and workflow-next-action.test.ts (Cases 10–13) against all four Review Dimensions.

Architecture: The routing loop correctly iterates active stages in canonical order, breaking on FAIL and IN_PROGRESS and short-circuiting for PASS. The upstream IN_PROGRESS guard (lines 483–489) is a defensive safety net; the loop's own ordering logic prevents it from being reached in practice, but it is harmless and adds resilience.

Maintainability: Logic is readable and consistent with the existing PM action priority block style. The `getOrderedActiveStages` + `resolvePrerequisite` helpers are correctly used to avoid duplicating canonical-ordering logic inline.

Best Practices: Import additions (PIPELINE_AGENT_MAP, getOrderedActiveStages) correctly pull from the single-source-of-truth pipeline-maps module — no constants are inlined. The auto_cancelled filter matches the pattern used by REVIEW_ABANDONED.
Performance: No concerns. The per-WP pipeline scan is O(stages × pipelines) with bounded small inputs — same profile as every other PM priority block.

Future Context: The `active_pipeline_stages ?? DEFAULT_PIPELINE_STAGES` fallback ensures backward compatibility with legacy 4-stage WPs that predate the per-WP stages field. The block cleanly slots into the 6-stage world.

comments.note: workflow-next-action.ts line 506: Renamed '--- Priority 4 / Fallback: WAIT ---' to '--- Final Fallback: WAIT ---'. workflow-next-action.ts lines 474–489: The upstream IN_PROGRESS guard (resolvePrerequisite → filter → at(-1)?.status === 'IN_PROGRESS') is logically unreachable in practice. The iteration loop breaks on any IN_PROGRESS mostRecent (line 480), so the upstream stage would have already triggered its own break before the current stage is evaluated. The guard is a harmless defensive net and consistent with the QA note — worth noting for future contributors so they understand why it exists. No change required.
